composition: Nominal chemical composition of the M2 steel (wt%, Fe balance, Table 1): Mn 20.04, Al 8.05, C 0.85, Si 0.18, Cr 0.42, Mo 0.34, V 0.62, Ti 0.09. The austenitic Fe–Mn–Al–C low-density steel is stabilized by Mn, Al and C; the M2 alloy differs from the Ti/V-free reference steel M1 mainly by a higher carbon level (0.61 → 0.85 wt%) plus the additions of 0.62 V and 0.09 Ti (M1 contains no V or Ti). The design intent of the Ti and V additions is that these strong carbide-forming elements precipitate (Ti, V)C carbides at high temperature and thereby modify the carbon distribution of the matrix, controlling where κ-carbides form during aging.
summary: M2-10 (also written "M2 aged 10 h") is the Ti- and V-modified Fe–Mn–Al–C austenitic low-density steel of this study after aging at 550 °C for 10 h. It is the intermediate aged condition of the M2 alloy (Fe–20.04Mn–8.05Al–0.85C–0.62V–0.09Ti, wt%) obtained by high-vacuum electric-arc melting, hot rolling 20→2 mm at 1000 °C, solution treatment at 1000 °C for 30 min (state M2-SS) and subsequent aging at 550 °C for 10 h, each cooling step by water quenching. The core question addressed with this sample is how strong carbide-forming Ti and V additions, by forming high-temperature (Ti, V)C carbides that act as carbon sinks, redistribute carbon in the matrix and thereby change κ-carbide precipitation from homogeneous to heterogeneous, so that strength can be raised without sacrificing work-hardening capacity.
